open_questions: Centroid is inconclusive (no sector with clear difference image) – on-target confirmation via ground-based transit would rule out a marginal blend
RUWE 1.322 and fit_b 0.9325 grazing solution leave system density consistency at -2.22 sigma; radial velocity or better light curve would test mass
Star shows spot variability (amplitude_ppm 8501) commensurate with Teff 3382 K and VARIABLE flag – activity affects precision but does not mimic this flat-bottomed 2.44 Rearth transit
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a flat-bottomed 13.3-day dip recurring over two sectors with only three transits, with no odd-even difference or secondary eclipse and no neighbour close enough to blend. The depth implies a 2.4 Earth-radius planet on a grazing orbit, well consistent with the M-dwarf star's size. The period matching about twice the star's rotation is expected to happen by chance around spotted stars and the light-curve shape, not the jitter, favours a planet.

reasons.why: Flat-bottomed shape favours a transit over a V-shaped binary eclipse despite high impact parameter.
No odd/even depth difference; 1.2 ratio with 0.1844 depth_difference and 1050 ppm difference is not significant.
No secondary eclipse at half phase (snr_at_half -1.482, best_brightening_snr 2.709) and phase_curve amplitude 446.6 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.08971 with chi2 7.527 dof 9 shows no binaries-phase signal.
Undiluted depth 4994 ppm and rp_over_rstar 0.07067 gives a 2.44 Earth-sized planet, well below stellar regime, positively favouring a planet.
No star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can produce the 4978 ppm dip, and target_found is true, so a blended eclipsing binary is unlikely despite inconclusive centroid.

Duration ratio 1.466 for observed_h 2.999 vs central_h 2.046 with fit_b 0.9325 and fit_log_density_ratio -2.22 explains long duration as a near-grazing but still planetary transit; Gaia radii not available but TIC rad 0.3168 gives rp_rearth 2.44 around a 0.2959 Msun M dwarf.

Period is about 2x rotation but phase_curve shows no large swing and shape is transit-like, so this is common chance alignment for spotted M dwarfs and does not favour spots/variability over a planet.

reasons.why: Depth steady across sectors (per_sector 4616 +/-633 ppm vs 5458 +/-593 ppm, chi2 0.942 dof 1) with 3 transits gives consistent dip despite low SNR 15.08 and top-share 0.4723, and there are no missing checks.
